extracted.intended_audience: PCI Registered Reports recommenders and prospective recommenders (PCI RR action editors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for recommenders overseeing Stage 1 and Stage 2 peer review of Registered Reports on the PCI RR platform, including assessment criteria, reviewer assignment, decision-making, and procedural rules. Intended to ensure consistent, rule-based evaluation and handling of RRs from triage through recommendation and appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triage assessment and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-review triage performed by Managing Board member(s) and a specialist recommender to judge submissions against the Stage 1 or Stage 2 review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Four possible outcomes: (1) Outright desk reject where submission falls a long way short of at least one review criterion; (2) Desk rejection with invitation to submit a revised manuscript where the submission is promising but significantly short of criteria; (3) Immediate in-depth review where the submission comes sufficiently close to meeting the criteria; (4) Immediate desk accept where a revised submission is judged to have sufficiently addressed reviewer concerns and satisfied the review criteria. The Managing Board oversees and can overrule recommender decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 Criterion 1A: Scientific validity of the research question(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which the research question is scientifically justifiable and answerable through quantitative or qualitative research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valid questions usually stem from theory/mathematics, application, or existing evidence base; should be defined precisely and fall within established ethical norms. Subjective judgments about importance, novelty, or timeliness are NOT relevant to PCI RR assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 Criterion 1B: Logic, rationale, and plausibility of proposed hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Coherence and credibility of any a priori hypotheses; hypotheses are optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where stated, hypotheses should be as precise as possible and follow from the research question/theory. A Stage 1 RR may instead propose estimation/measurement without specific hypotheses. Preliminary data evaluation is included in this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 Criterion 1C: Soundness and feasibility of methodology and analysis pipeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Validity of study procedures and analyses, including critical design features and appropriateness of analysis plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess internal/external validity, blinding, randomisation, rules for data inclusion/exclusion, suitability of pilot data. For inferential designs include sampling plan rigour (statistical power analysis or Bayesian alternative) and rationale for priors or smallest effect size of interest. For programmatic RRs assess robustness/substance of separate study components (see programmatic guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 Criterion 1D: Methodological detail sufficient for replication and to prevent undisclosed flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which the Stage 1 protocol contains sufficient detail to closely replicate procedures and analyses and to prevent analytic flexibility or overfitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods sections should be longer/more detailed than a regular manuscript and clearly structured. Protocols should precisely link research questions, hypotheses, sampling plans, analysis plans, and contingent interpretation. Authors are encouraged to include a design summary table. Blinded analyst approaches are acceptable provided the blinding procedure is reproducibly detailed and robust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 Criterion 1E: Prespecified outcome-neutral quality checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether authors have considered sufficient outcome-neutral conditions (e.g., absence of floor/ceiling effects; positive controls; other quality checks) to ensure results can test stated hypotheses or answer research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcome-neutral tests must be pre-specified and independent of main hypotheses. Examples: positive controls/manipulation checks in experiments; parallel measurements in observational studies. Such checks vary by field and may not always be applicable. The guide provides an illustrative example (Galileo spacecraft study).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 Criterion 2A: Data meet approved outcome-neutral criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the data are able to test the authors’ proposed hypotheses (or answer the question) by passing the pre-specified outcome-neutral criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses data quality according to pre-specified checks in Stage 1. Failure of critical outcome-neutral tests can, in severe cases, lead to Stage 2 rejection; the severity and context determine the recommender/reviewers' judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 Criterion 2B: Consistency of introduction, rationale and hypotheses with Stage 1
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the introduction, rationale and stated hypotheses are the same as in the approved Stage 1 submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aside from tense changes, typographic/factual corrections, and error corrections, these elements must remain identical. Authors must submit a tracked-changes version at Stage 2 to make any changes transparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 Criterion 2C: Adherence to registered study procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the authors adhered precisely to the registered protocol and study procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deviations after IPA due to unforeseen circumstances require immediate consultation with the recommender before data collection completion. Minor changes may be permitted at recommender discretion and reported in Stage 2; substantial changes require withdrawal and resubmission as a new Stage 1. All preregistered analyses must be reported unless collectively agreed to be flawed, in which case they may be mentioned but omitted from results with justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 Criterion 2D: Justification and soundness of unregistered exploratory analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, whether any unregistered exploratory/post hoc analyses are justified, methodologically sound, and informative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploratory analyses must be clearly identified (e.g., separate Results heading), justified, and appropriately caveated. Authors should avoid basing conclusions entirely on unregistered analyses. New analytic approaches or unexpected findings can justify exploratory work, but transparency is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 Criterion 2E: Conclusions justified by the evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the authors’ conclusions are warranted by the data and evidence presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether claims in Discussion, Abstract, and elsewhere are supported by the evidence. PCI RR recommendations are never based on perceived importance, novelty, or conclusiveness of results. Recommenders should also check data/code sharing statements in the submission report survey and verify sharing if stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigning reviewers: numbers, conflicts, scope, and co-reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommenders invite and assign expert reviewers, aiming for field-specialist assessment and avoiding conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to assign 3 field-specialist reviewers (never less than 2) for the first in-depth Stage 1 submission; this typically requires inviting 5–10 reviewers. Avoid reviewers with clear conflicts (recent co-publication, joint funding, same institution). Authors may recommend up to five independent reviewers and oppose up to five; recommender must ensure suggested reviewers are independent. Recommender can serve as one of the reviewers if a field-specialist with no conflict. Recommenders can also invite reviewers for specific parts (statistics, code) even if they lack domain expertise. Co-reviewing by juniors is allowed; juniors should be invited as separate reviewers to receive credit, with instructions on how to record joint reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer timelines, continuity and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations for review turnaround times and the importance of retaining reviewers between stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For standard workflow, reviewers are requested to complete assessments within 14 days of accepting. Extensions are negotiable. Recommenders should invite the same reviewers back at Stage 2 where possible. For programmatic RRs anticipate reviewer loss and recruit more reviewers at Stage 1 to increase the chance that at least 2 will assess the project through to completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review outcomes (Reject, Invitation to revise, Accept/IPA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Possible recommender judgments after peer review and their triggers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject when major uncorrectable flaws require a new programme of work. Invitation to revise when shortcomings are correctable and a comprehensive response to reviewers is required. Accept (IPA at Stage 1 or Stage 2 acceptance) when submissions meet the relevant criteria. Managing Board oversees and may confirm or overrule recommender decisions. Effective triage reduces post-review outright rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercising recommender judgment and handling reviewer disagreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommenders use reviews as advice but must apply their own judgment in recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consensus among reviewers is desirable but not required. Recommenders should read all reviews and the submission before deciding. For minor revisions, aim to assess at desk to avoid overburdening reviewers. Where reviews conflict, the recommender should guide authors toward resolution and may consult the Managing Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing, returning, or discarding low-quality or abusive reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling reviews that violate the PCI RR code of conduct or contain no useful information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parts of reviews judged to violate the code of conduct may be returned to reviewers for editing before inclusion in the open record. Entire reviews that contain no value may be discarded. Recommenders can flag content unnecessary for authors to address and may contact reviewers to request improved reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional recommender assessments at Stage 1 and recommendation text requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: At Stage 1 IPA (and at Stage 2 acceptance) recommenders perform basic metadata assessments and write a short recommendation text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess: research discipline(s); whether research is quantitative/qualitative/mixed; evidential standard reached for hypotheses (power, Bayes factors, other); level of bias control (recommender's designation overrules authors’ self-declaration); whether manuscript reports meta-analysis/systematic review/map; whether proposed research falls within typical ethical norms. Recommendation text: a short summary (a few hundred words) describing context and why article was accepted; cite all information and comments used to reach the decision, in addition to peer reviews. Recommendation and editorial correspondence are published by PCI RR no later than Stage 2 acceptance. Recommenders may contact authors to request clarifications to make these assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using AI to generate recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommenders must not use AI (LLMs) to generate recommendation texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If AI is used to generate recommendation text there is a risk of the text being rejected by the Managing Board and the recommender being banned. Recommenders may use AI only to translate, correct and improve text, not to create recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open review policy and publication of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI RR publishes reviews and editorial correspondence for recommended manuscripts, with rules on anonymity and timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All Stage 1 and Stage 2 reviews, recommender decision letters, and the Stage 1 recommendation are published on PCI RR no later than Stage 2 acceptance. Reviewers may sign or remain anonymous (exception: if an author is a Managing Board member, all reviews must be signed). Authors can opt to have Stage 1 materials published at point of Stage 1 IPA. Reviews of rejected submissions are not published. Authors and reviewers are asked not to self-publish review content during the process or after rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure and permissible grounds for authors to appeal a rejection by PCI RR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals must be emailed within 30 days and must clearly state why the decision should be changed. Appealable grounds: (a) identification of factual errors by reviewers/recommender that had a major impact on the decision, or (b) substantiated claim of unfair treatment/bias. Appeals meeting criteria are reviewed by a panel (the recommender + two Managing Board members) and decided by majority vote; final decisions are final. Appeals for other reasons are denied without further consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prespecifying quality checks and handling failures
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance and difficulty of deciding, at Stage 1, the outcome-neutral quality checks that must be passed to consider the experiment adequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcome-neutral checks must be independent of research hypotheses and may include positive controls, tests of intervention fidelity, reality checks, attainment of benchmarks, etc. Failure of such tests can justify Stage 2 rejection depending on severity. Non-fatal failures may be mitigated by corroborating evidence or may themselves be important findings if they reveal unreliability of the checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: No relitigation (goalpost shifting) of approved Stage 1 methodology at Stage 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 2 reviewers should not relitigate the rationale or methods that were approved at Stage 1 merely because results are unexpected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except in rare cases where all parties agree a major flaw was missed, approved methodology cannot be a basis for rejection at Stage 2. Reviewers may suggest post hoc analyses but these are not required unless necessary to satisfy Stage 2 criteria (e.g., to justify conclusions under Criterion 2E). Recommenders should prevent demands for unnecessary post hoc work driven by disagreement with results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible changes between Stage 1 and Stage 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Which textual and substantive changes are allowed between IPA (Stage 1 acceptance) and Stage 2 submission, and how deviations must be handled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed changes: future-to-past tense shifts, updating Abstract to include results/conclusions, title changes to reflect results, correction of typographical or factual errors, adding/removing authors without PCI approval. Deviations from accepted methodology must be documented in Methods with a footnote explaining nature/reason. Any substantial procedural changes require consultation with the recommender before data collection; substantial alterations require readmission to Stage 1 or resubmission. All textual changes to approved parts must be highlighted as tracked changes in Stage 2 (or linked to a tracked-changes version). New literature after IPA belongs in the Discussion, not Introduction. No changes to research question, rationale, or hypotheses are permitted at Stage 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic Registered Reports: requirements and boundaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for programmatic Stage 1 RRs that prespecify multiple Stage 2 outputs from a single protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmatic RRs must meet usual RR criteria and make clear how components fit together. Must prespecify which parts will produce separate Stage 2 articles; reviewers/recommenders evaluate validity and contribution of each component (per 1C). Stage 2 manuscripts correspond to specific Stage 1 components and must include statement that current manuscript is part of larger protocol (public URL), cite previous Stage 2 outputs from same protocol, and note components awaiting completion or rejected/withdrawn. If registered under temporary private embargo at IPA, embargo is released when the first Stage 2 manuscript is received; authors wanting to avoid this should submit separate regular RRs. Withdrawn Registrations: entire components planned as separate Stage 2 outputs can be withdrawn without affecting IPA of remaining components, but parts of a single component cannot be withdrawn without withdrawing the entire RR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard review vs Scheduled review track
rubrics_metrics.description: Two routes for Stage 1 peer review: standard detailed submission vs. scheduled expedited process using a 1-page snapshot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard review: submit full Stage 1 manuscript, first round ~4–6 weeks. Scheduled review: submit 1-page template snapshot for triage; if suitable the recommender sends snapshot to reviewers and arranges review during a narrow 1-week window at least 6 weeks later; authors prepare full manuscript in the interim. Scheduled review requires using the PCI RR 1-page snapshot template; submissions not using it will not be considered. Both tracks available for Regular and Programmatic RRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with late or non-responding reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for recommender actions when reviewers fail to deliver reviews or are non-contactable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-responsive reviewers often require finding replacements and can delay decisions by weeks. As insurance, recommenders are advised to assign four reviewers for each Stage 1 submission so a decision could be issued if one or two reviews are missing. Be flexible about short extensions. If a sufficient number of original Stage 1 reviewers are unavailable for Stage 2, a recommender can invite new Stage 2 reviewers who must assess according to Stage 2 criteria and not relitigate Stage 1 approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seeking statistical advice and specialist methodological reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to obtain statistical or other methodological expertise during Stage 1 review when required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many Stage 1 submissions benefit from review of proposed statistical methods by field specialists or statisticians. Recommenders lacking specialist expertise should seek statistical assessment. The Managing Board can assist in recruiting appropriate reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data, code, and materials availability (PCI RR TOP guidelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectation that authors make study data, digital materials and code publicly available unless legal/ethical restrictions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadly requires public availability of data/materials/code; if restrictions exist, authors must explain the process by which requesters can obtain materials and any conditions. Recommenders should direct authors to the TOP policy and consult the Managing Board on specific cases. Recommenders should verify declared sharing where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommender training, declaration of interests, and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for prospective recommenders to ensure minimum understanding of role, policies, and potential conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective recommenders must read PCI RR policies, Guide to Reviewers, and RR overview materials, complete a declaration of interests, and pass the PCI RR entrance test to achieve certification before handling their first assignment. The entrance test can be taken multiple times and requires scoring at least 63 out of 66 points (95%).
